data.name: Jehoshaphat
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Jehoshaphat means 'God has judged'. In the Bible, Jehoshaphat was a king of Judah who sought the Lord's guidance and experienced great victories. Despite his successes, he was warned by the prophet Hanani for disobeying God's commandments and was later attacked by his enemies.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name reflecting trust in God's judgment and guidance.
data.numerology_meaning: Intuition, spiritual growth, and material success.

in_hebrew.name: יהושפט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יהושפט (Yehoshafat) הוא שם עברי המשמר את המשמעות של 'צדק יה' . שם זה מוזכר במקרא (2 מלכים 15:24, 2 מלכים 22:2) כשם מלך יהודה. יהושפט נחשב כספיריטואל, אמיץ ומוכשר .

in_greek.name: Ιεχωσαφάτ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιεχωσαφάτ είναι ονομασία από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα, που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι δικαιοσύνη'. Ο Ιεχωσαφάτ αναφέρεται στην Καινή Διαθήκη (Β' Βασιλέων 15:24, Β' Βασιλέων 22:2) ως βασιλιάς του Ισραήλ. Ο Ιεχωσαφάτ θεωρείται ως πνευματικός, γενναίος και ικανός άνθρωπος.

in_latin.name: Jehoshaphat
in_latin.long_meaning: Jehoshaphat est nomen Hebraicum, quod significat 'Iustitia Domini'. Jehoshaphat in Veteri Testamento (2 Regum 15:24, 2 Regum 22:2) citatur ut rex Israel. Jehoshaphat habet significatum spiritual, fortis et capax.

in_english.name: Jehoshaphat
in_english.meaning: God is His justice, righteous king of Judah
in_english.long_meaning: Jehoshaphat is a Hebrew name that means 'God is His justice'. He is mentioned in the Bible (2 Kings 15:24, 2 Kings 22:2) as the king of Judah. Jehoshaphat is considered a spiritual, brave, and capable person. He is also associated with being wise and having a strong faith in God. In Christian tradition, Jehoshaphat is seen as a symbol of righteousness, justice, and faithfulness.

biblical_reference.note: Jehoshaphat is mentioned in the book of 2 Kings as the king of Judah.

saint_reference.note: King Jehoshaphat is revered as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church for his faithfulness to God and his righteousness as a ruler.

data.cultural_impact: Jehoshaphat's name remains significant in Jewish and Christian history as a symbol of seeking God's guidance and judgment in times of crisis. His reign is noted for his commitment to religious reform, expanding the territory of Judah, and establishing a league of alliance with other ancient kingdoms.
data.spiritual_significance: Jehoshaphat's name serves as an reminder of the importance of seeking God's judgment and guidance, even in times of great success or victory. As a religious reformer, he demonstrates the importance of staying faithful to God's commandments, despite the pressures and distractions of ruling a nation. Additionally, Jehoshaphat's life story teaches us about the consequences of disobedience to God and the importance of repentance.
